Fewer insects mean less pollination for fruit and vegetables.
Many birds as a result lack food.
In Switzerland there are around 600 species of wild bee.
Native wild flowers in the garden help insects.

abschnitte.text: In **2017**, the so-called **Krefeld study** was published. An association from Krefeld in Germany had caught and weighed flying insects in protected areas over almost three decades. The **insect biomass** had fallen by more than three quarters in that time. The study drew attention to the problem around the world. Other studies also show a decline in many groups of insects.

There is not just one cause. Many **flower meadows**, hedges and wetlands have disappeared. **Pesticides** from farming also harm insects that are not pests. Meadows that are mown often and heavily fertilised have **hardly any flowers**, so butterflies find little food there. In addition there is **artificial light** at night: it attracts many insects, which then circle the lamp until they are exhausted.

Insects are important **pollinators**. If they are missing, there is less fruit, fewer berries and fewer seeds. That is a problem for farming. In addition, insects are **food** for many animals. Swallows, tits and other birds feed their young on insects. Bats, hedgehogs and frogs also depend on them.

Everyone can help. In the garden or on the balcony you can sow **native wild flowers**. One corner can be left wild, with leaves, branches and stones. An **insect hotel** offers wild bees **nesting places**. At night you should switch off unnecessary light. In Switzerland there are **around 600 species of wild bee**, and many of them depend on this kind of help.

gewusst: In the Krefeld study, volunteers collected insects in traps for almost 30 years.
Most animal species in the world are insects.

teile.einleitung: Currants are small, sharp-tasting berries that grow in bunches on bushes. In Switzerland they are often called “Meertrübeli”. There are red, black and white varieties.
wichtigste: Currants can be red, black or white.
They hang in small bunches on the bush.
In German they are named after St John’s Day.
In Switzerland people often say “Meertrübeli”.
The blackcurrant is also called cassis.
Blackcurrants contain a lot of vitamin C.

abschnitte.text: Currants grow on **bushes** that reach about one to two metres in height. The berries hang in **small bunches** on thin stalks. There are **red**, **black** and **white** currants. The white ones are a pale form of the red. The gooseberry is a close relative.

The first berries ripen around **St John’s Day** on 24 June. That is where the German name “Johannisbeere” comes from. In Switzerland people often say **“Meertrübeli”** or simply “Trübeli”, because the berries look like little grapes. In Austria they are called “Ribisel”, after the Latin name Ribes.

Redcurrants taste **sharp** and refreshing. They are eaten raw with sugar, in cakes or as jelly and jam. The blackcurrant is also called **cassis**. It has a strong, tart taste and contains especially much **vitamin C**. It is made into juice, syrup and jam.

The berries are small and hang on many stalks. Picking them off one by one takes a long time. With a **fork** it goes much faster: you run the prongs along the stalk, and the berries drop off. Currants are delicate and should be eaten or processed soon after harvesting.

gewusst: Blackcurrants contain more vitamin C than lemons.
Currant bushes bear plenty of fruit only a few years after planting.

teile.einleitung: The hydrangea is a popular garden shrub with large, round balls of flowers. What is especially interesting is that some hydrangeas bloom blue or pink depending on the soil.
wichtigste: Hydrangeas are shrubs and usually grow about one to two metres tall.
Many have large, round flower heads like balls.
Hydrangeas need a great deal of water.
They like best to stand in partial shade.
The garden hydrangea comes from Japan.
Hydrangeas flower in summer.

abschnitte.text: The flowers of many hydrangeas look like **big balls**. Each ball is made up of many small flowers. Hydrangeas bloom from **early summer** until late summer, and the flowers last a very long time. In **autumn** the balls of flowers often dry on the shrub and change colour. You can cut them for **dried bouquets**.

Hydrangeas need a great deal of **water**. Their scientific name **Hydrangea** means roughly **water vessel**. If the soil is too dry, they let their leaves and flowers **droop**. After watering they often recover quickly. In blazing sun they easily go limp. They feel most comfortable in **partial shade**.

In some hydrangeas the colour depends on the **soil**. In **acidic soil**, where the plant can take up **aluminium**, they flower **blue**. In **limy soil**, the flowers turn **pink**. Gardeners sometimes add special fertilisers to get blue flowers. White hydrangeas, by contrast, do not change their colour.

The popular **garden hydrangea** originally comes from **Japan**. From there, plant lovers brought it to Europe. Today it grows in many gardens and on balconies in Switzerland. Hydrangeas grow as **shrubs** with several woody shoots. They usually reach about one to two metres in height.

gewusst: In some hydrangeas, the showy coloured parts are not petals at all, but sepals.
The leaves and flowers of the hydrangea are mildly poisonous and do not belong in the mouth.

teile.einleitung: Hyaline cells are large, empty cells in the small leaves of peat mosses that fill with water. They make peat mosses into huge water stores and are one reason why raised bogs stay so wet.
wichtigste: Hyaline cells store water.
“Hyaline” means transparent like glass, from the Greek hyalos for glass.
Fully grown hyaline cells are dead and have no living contents.
Between them lies a network of green cells containing chlorophyll.
Water flows in through pores in the cell wall.
Ring-shaped or spiral reinforcements stop the cells from collapsing.

abschnitte.text: A small leaf of a **peat moss** consists of only one layer of cells. Under the microscope you can see two kinds of cell. The large, empty ones are called **hyaline cells**. Between them runs a narrow network of **cells containing chlorophyll**. These green cells contain **chloroplasts** and carry out **photosynthesis**. The hyaline cells are responsible for the water.

The word **hyaline** comes from the Greek **hyalos**, meaning glass. The cells are colourless and transparent. As they mature, they lose their living contents, the **protoplast**. All that is left is the **cell wall** as a hollow space. It is exactly this empty space that can take up a lot of water.

The hyaline cells have round **pores** in their wall. Water flows rapidly and directly in through these openings. So that the empty cells do not collapse when they dry out, **ring-shaped or spiral reinforcements** are built into the wall. They support the cell like rings in a hose. In this way the stores are always ready for new water.

When the hyaline cells are filled with **water**, they are transparent. The green of the other cells then shines through. When a cushion of peat moss dries out, the cells fill with **air**. The air scatters the light, and the moss looks **whitish**. The **white moss** (Leucobryum glaucum) also has large, empty cells in its many-layered leaves. That is why its cushions look light grey to bluish white.

gewusst: Thanks to the hyaline cells, peat mosses can take up many times their own dry weight in water.
Because of their absorbency, peat mosses used to be used as dressing material for wounds.
